pr.body:
Bean `l4ay` (parent `fs43`). Follow-up bean: `r5wu`.

## Owner rulings (2026-10-03, verbatim)
- "todos = subgraph node + todo content nodes" → option 1, "and make pattern for declared repo branches (and declared dir subgraphs)"
- "It's the same pattern. One of them is mounting the directory while one of them is mounting a branch. Another mount type could come in the future. A sub graph declares where it's getting its content.. It could also be a graph database in the future. That same information can be overwritten by the harness instance config. Update skills process processes and tools"

## What this does
A directory-backed subgraph and a branch-backed subgraph are now one concept. Each declared subgraph says where its content comes from (its **source**). There is one resolver, and publishers use the declared Subgraph node as their container.

### Schema: `cat-harness/schemas/subgraph-source.ts`
- `directories[].source` is a discriminated union on `kind`.
- `{ kind: "directory" }` is the default, and also what an absent `source` means.
- `{ kind: "branch", branch, keyedBy: "commit" | "tip" }` means the content lives on a branch.
- A future kind such as `graph-db` is added as a new union member. That makes it a compile error at every `switch` that has not handled it yet.
- Branch names are still declared once, in `special-branches.json`. The resolver attaches the matching row (exact name or family, legacy names included).

### How the old fields map
| old | new |
|---|---|
| `storage: { branch, keyedBy }` (#1764, on main; `tip` added by #1937) | `source: { kind: "branch", branch, keyedBy }`. `storage` stays as the **legacy spelling**. The resolver reads either field, reports `declaredIn: "storage"`, and **refuses an entry that carries both**. A `qa` subgraph keyed by `tip` is refused whichever field it is set through. |
| presence checks reading `storage?.branch` (`materialiseDirectories`, `check:declared-dirs`, `audit:coverage`) | `contentIsOffCheckout(entry)`, which honours both fields. |
| `qa-store.ts` reading `storage` | **Unchanged.** It is #1937's file, and moving it onto the resolver is that session's call. |

### Override in the instance config, matched on id
`<instance>.config.json` → `subgraphSources: { "<dir-id>": <source> }`. The checkout root's config has the last word.

### One resolver
`declaredSubgraph(start, id)` in `schemas/harness-config.ts`. Precedence: config override, then `source`, then `storage`, then `directory`. The result carries `declaredIn`. The KG export, the publishers, the CLI and (as proposed on #1957) `branch-store mount`/`push` all call it.

### JSON-LD
- Every Subgraph node in the KG export now carries `contentSource`.
- **Vocabulary is reused where possible:**
  - `contentSource` is `dcterms:source`;
  - the scoped `kind` is `dcterms:type`;
  - the scoped `branch` is `dcterms:identifier`.
- **Two terms are minted** and glossed in `vocabulary.ts`: `keyedBy` and `sourceDeclaredIn`. No published vocabulary says how entries are keyed on a branch, or which configuration layer gave an answer.
- A branch hosted on GitHub gets an `@id` equal to its tree URL. Any other forge gets a blank node, because a link that 404s is worse than none.
- `storedOn` was considered and not minted: `dcterms:source` already means "the resource this one is derived from", and that covers a future graph-db source too.

### The pattern: `scripts/subgraph-node.ts`
- `subgraphIri(docIri, id)` is pinned equal to kg-export's `makeIri(doc, "directory", id)`.
- `subgraphContainer` uses the declared node's IRI as the container `@id`, typed `Subgraph`, with `hasPart`.
- `memberOf` adds `inSubgraph` to each member. That is kg-export's existing term for this edge, and it expands to `dcterms:isPartOf`.
- No parallel collection node is minted.
- `subgraphPublicationFindings` is the check.

### Applied to todos
- `todos.jsonld`'s container is the declared `todos` Subgraph node: `<base>/folio-assistant/folio-assistant.jsonld#directory/todos`. The checkout root instance declares `todos`.
- `TodoGraph` → `schema:Collection` is gone.
- Each todo, in the graph and in its own document, gains `inSubgraph`.
- **The `@graph` array and every todo `@id` are unchanged.** I commented on #1953 with exactly what changed for `fetchTodoGraph`: nothing it reads.
- `docs-site.yml` and `feature-staging.yml` now export the checkout root's graph, so the container `@id` dereferences.
- `check:published-instance-exports` now names a sidecar by the instance's **stub** rather than the directory basename. The two differ for `.`.
- Verified with `publish:verify` (#1950's `jsonld-object-links` and `jsonld-own-base`) over `todos.jsonld`, the per-todo documents, and both instance graphs. All passed.

### Skills, processes and tools (the owner's "update skills process processes and tools")
- **Skill `directory-conventions`:** new section §"Where a subgraph gets its content — `source`", plus the STRICT subsection §"Publishing a subgraph's contents — the declared Subgraph node is the container", plus a new checklist item.
- **Skill `content-context-and-state-graphs`:** new section §"The layer is not the source". `todos` is `state` whether it is mounted from a directory or from a branch.
- **Process `processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn`:** resolve the source once, then a gateway on kind. `directory` is used in place, `branch` mounts the tip, and an unknown kind is refused. It is indexed on the publication-workflow page.
- **Tool `subgraph-resolve`:** `bun run subgraph:resolve <id> [--json] | --all`.
- **Interface for #1957:** posted at https://github.com/litlfred/folio-assistant/pull/1957#issuecomment-5967425740. The mount/push dispatch on kind is #1957's change; its files are untouched here.

### Gates
- `subgraph-source.test.ts` tests the union, precedence, the legacy mapping, both refusals, and the special-branch lookup. It also asserts that **every subgraph the checkout declares resolves, and that each branch source names a declared branch**.
- `subgraph-node.test.ts` checks that every adopting publisher passes `subgraphPublicationFindings` against the declared node, and mutation-checks each failure the check is meant to catch.

## Declarations affected
- Every `directories[]` entry, in every instance, gains an **optional** `source`, so no existing declaration changes.
- #1949's new `merge-queue` → `beans/queue/` (`state`, `recordsWork: true`) is covered as it stands: absent `source` means `directory`. If it later moves to a branch, it declares `source: { kind: "branch", … }` with a branch row in `special-branches.json`.
- #1937's intended `beans/` and `todos/` flips can be written either as `storage: { branch, keyedBy: "tip" }` or as `source: { kind: "branch", … }`. **Prefer `source`.**

## Audit: other publishers that mint their own container (not converted here, bean `r5wu`)
- `fsh-guts-export.ts`: its own `FshGutsGraph` container; its nodes carry no `inSubgraph`.
- `schemas/role-graph.ts` `toJsonLd`: a `RoleGraph` container.
- `glossary-export.ts`: a `skos:ConceptScheme` for `swimlane-glossary`. This is a real SKOS concept, so it should be linked to the Subgraph, not replaced by it.
- `content/pipeline/gen-library-jsonld.ts`: `SourceDocument` manifests with no `inSubgraph` to `library`.
- `content/pipeline/gen-site-jsonld.ts`: site pages with no `inSubgraph`. A page's `contains` is document structure and stays.
- beans and qa: plain-JSON indexes today. Each must follow the pattern when it becomes JSON-LD.

## Order
This PR targets `main` and depends on neither #1937 nor #1957. Because of the `storage` mapping, it and #1937 can land in either order. #1957 adopts the interface after this lands.

## Checklist
- [x] `source` union, plus the mapping from `storage`
- [x] the instance config overrides by id; one resolver
- [x] Subgraph JSON-LD node carries `contentSource`
- [x] `subgraphContainer` / `memberOf`; todos converted
- [x] gates (`subgraph-source.test.ts`, `subgraph-node.test.ts`)
- [x] skills, process and tool
- [x] audit of the other publishers, plus follow-up bean `r5wu`
- [x] #1957 interface comment; #1953 reader check
- [x] `publish:verify` on the outputs
- [ ] CI green
